title: Solitude
hookLine: the forest's quiet, and the calm of fewer ties (Bodhicaryavatara 8)
tomorrow: why hold on so tight to people who'll leave?

lines: THE CAFÉ IS STILL IN YOUR HEAD.
cards: Noise-canceling headphones on, and the café is still in your head: the group chat, the deadline, the thing someone said at lunch. Some quiet can be bought. Some can't: you can close every app and still hear all of them.
When life gets loud, where does Shantideva go? His chapter on meditation, dhyana, begins with a surprising first step. Not a technique.
Not a posture. He walks out of town.

teach.b: He praises the forest: trees that say nothing unkind, deer and birds that make easy company, a place where the mind isn't pulled a dozen ways by other people's wanting. He's honest about why.
Ties to praise, to crowds, to keeping up, scatter attention, and a scattered mind can't settle.
The Sanskrit word is viveka, seclusion, and it's room, not escape. He isn't running from people; his whole guide is about living for them.

He's making space to come back clearer. His poem pictures the woods; for most of us the shape is smaller: a walk without the phone, an hour with the door closed, a bench under a tree. Now look back down the path.
Envy, answered: their praise is fine. Effort, defined: delight in the good. Its disguise: busy isn't effort.
Its support: rest is a strength. Its start: into the pool. Its momentum: lifted by the wind.
Six lines, and a seventh today: the quiet of the forest, where all of them have room to grow.

how: Buddhist monastics have long kept forest and retreat traditions; lay Buddhists often take a day or an hour of quiet practice away from screens and errands.

o: a punishment of being left out by others
living alone for good, away from all people
the quiet of fewer ties, where the mind has room

games.q: the forest's quiet — tap the pairs.
p: an hour with the door closed

s: Shantideva praises the forest for trees that say nothing unkind
deer, birds and trees make easy company; the mind isn't pulled by other people's wanting.
in the poem, solitude means escaping people for good
it's room for the mind to settle; his whole guide is about living for others.

games.q: a loud house, an essay due, and one free hour. which choice fits the quiet of the forest?
o: an hour with the door closed and the phone in another room.
stay in the kitchen; noise doesn't matter if you're disciplined.
wait for a free weekend at a cabin before starting.
games.why: the forest's point is room for the mind. for most people the shape is small: a closed door, a walk, a bench.

practice: Close your eyes, or rest them on the floor. Let the sounds around you be the forest: a fan, the traffic, the hum of a fridge. Don't push them away; just stop answering them, the way trees don't answer the wind.
Stay in that quiet as long as the sit runs.

wordCard.voice: Solitude: in Shantideva's meditation chapter, the quiet of fewer ties, a forest where the mind has room.

orig.note: Sanskrit: separation, seclusion; solitude that gives the mind room.

carryVoice: A line to keep: the quiet of the forest, which fits in an hour with the door closed. A week, gathered.

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 8.1-8.4 and 8.25-8.28 (seclusion of body and mind; the forest, trees that say nothing unkind)
